paragraphs: Transparent Language sells online language learning that organizations license for their members, students or staff. Public and academic libraries license a version that gives their communities materials in more than 100 languages. Businesses, state and local government agencies and non-profits license the same catalog. A separate platform called CL-150 serves U.S. federal government and partner nation agencies. A schools edition lets K-12 and higher-ed teachers manage classes and report on student activity.

Administrators can watch learner activity in real time and report on platform usage. Instructors can create and assign custom lessons in any language, at any level, on any topic. The company says its technology is built to work with other courses and curricula, not only its own. It describes drawing on work by experts in linguistics and neuroscience when designing its products.

The about page lists government personnel, the military, public libraries, universities and business executives among the people who use it. It says the products are available in thousands of libraries, corporate organizations and educational institutions. Press releases note a highest award for two years running in the Modern Library Awards from LibraryWorks. Case studies on the site cover institutions including the United States Military Academy at West Point.

quote.text: We make their challenge our mission: to train language faster with more reliable results.
